title: How AI is genuinely changing the workflow for a solo dev (and where the human touch still does all the heavy lifting)
author: MaksTheGamesDev
selftext:
As a solo developer working on my cozy airship management game, I’ve been experimenting a lot with AI as part of my toolchain. And honestly? It’s been a massive game-changer allowing me to prototype visuals and mechanics much faster than if I were doing everything purely from scratch in image editors or writing all the code alone.

However, it’s definitely not a "one-click magic" button. Not for me definately. Here is what the reality actually looks like in my workflow:

* **For Code & Logic:** I still have to write very precise, well-thought-out prompts for game mechanics, and I constantly find myself manually refactoring, debugging, and wiring things up inside Unity. I started experimenting with Unity CLI recently, and while it gives a slight speed boost to things I used to do by hand, deep configuration and implementation still require deep human oversight. its like having your own june dev forking for you all the time (as long as you have tokens, hehe)
* **For Art & Visuals:** AI-generated images mostly serve as advanced concept art or raw material rather than final, ready-to-use assets. A lot of the time, I take generated pieces into Photoshop, iterate through multiple rounds of edits, combine different parts, paint over details, and remove unwanted elements. I wold like to type "make game nice" and have work done. But dont have that yet (not hehe, as a lot of manual work still needed)

In short, AI isn't doing the work *for* me — it’s acting like an accelerator that helps bridge the gap between an idea and a working prototype. I would say +40% of speed in coding (+20 in making code I know and +20 in reserching ideas instead of googling). And about +50 in making "not so bad looking art" as, here I have not so much skills and expertise.

What do you think about results? And do you know how make art feel better and in one style with less manual polishing? Let me know in the comments!
